(This evening through Sunday)...
Issued at 220 PM EST Sun Nov 8 2026

Surface analysis this afternoon shows low pressure over Ontario with 
a trailing cold front across the Great Lakes to IL and MO. This was 
a dry front as no precip or cloud cover was found near the front. A 
ridge of high pressure was found over the plains. GOES19 shows sunny 
skies across Indiana. Water Vapor shows strong ridging in place over 
the Rockies with a trough in place over the Great Lakes. This was 
resulting in NW flow aloft and subsidence was seen IN and IL. Dew 
points across Indiana were in the mid 30s.

Tonight...

Quiet and cool weather will be expected tonight. The northwest flow 
is expected to remain in place aloft as the ridging over the Rockies 
pushes east and subsidence continues to build across Central 
Indiana. The surface high pressure system to the west will also 
build east into Indiana. Forecast soundings and time heights show a 
dry column. Thus clear skies will be expected. Some Patchy fog, 
particularly in rural or low lying areas cannot be ruled out as dew 
point depressions may reach 3F or less. Look for lows in the middle 
and upper 30s.

Monday through Tuesday...

Quiet and dry weather is expected to start the work week. Upper 
ridging is expected to reside over Indiana and the Great Lakes on 
Monday, providing little in the way of forcing. Meanwhile the 
surface high pressure will remain in place across the area. Again 
forecast soundings show a dry column. With southwest winds expected 
highs in the lower 60s should be reached.

The cool and dry weather will continue on Monday night through 
Tuesday Night as northwest flow aloft slowly become a bit zonal by 
late Tuesday Night. A strong area of surface high pressure will 
remain in place across the Mississippi and Ohio River Valleys along 
with the deep south. Little to no moisture will be available through 
this time and forecast soundings continue to show a dry column. 
Westerly winds through the period will allow for a a continued slow 
and small warming trend with warmer lows in the low to mid 40s on 
Monday Night and highs in the middle 60s on Tuesday.
and
Wednesday through Sunday... 

Weather conditions across the Ohio Valley late this week through the 
weekend will largely be dictated by the expected development of an 
amplified mid to upper ridge across the Western CONUS. Ensemble 
guidance is in large agreement for a very amplified ridge to develop 
along the Intermountain West Tuesday through Friday of next week, of 
which will have cascading impacts to central Indiana. Initially, 
upper level height depletion within modest CVA upstream of the ridge 
will aid in a deepening trough over the Mississippi Valley by 
Wednesday. This will likely lead to lee cyclogenesis downstream of 
central Rockies late Tuesday into Wednesday. There is still modest 
ensemble spread on the specifics of this surface low, but there is 
general agreement on the low nearing maturity over the Great Lakes 
to Ohio Valley sometime late Wednesday into Wednesday night.

Specific impacts to central Indiana will vary depending on low 
placement and magnitude, but regardless of outcome, general 
probability of precipitation will increase throughout Wednesday. 
Given strong dynamics of the mid to upper pattern, along with 
potential for veering flow aloft ahead of the low, there is some 
potential for severe weather next Wednesday. That said, confidence 
is not high at this time with still a wide variety of potential 
outcomes and thermodynamic solutions. 

Continued amplified ridging upstream of the aforementioned low will 
likely lead to a strong push of cold air into the Ohio Valley on 
Thursday as the low deepens and prolonged NW flow develops from the 
Canadian Plains into the region. Ensemble are still fairly spread on 
the axis of this cold air, but in general 850mb temps are expected to 
drop well below freezing of which should push highs into the 40s 
with lows in the 20s Thursday night through Saturday. Strong 
temperature differences between the lake and low level air mass will 
likely lead to, a few weakly forced snow/rain showers over central 
Indiana Thursday night and Friday, but QPF is expected to be 
minimal. 

Late Saturday through Sunday, the longwave pattern will being to 
progress with WAA entering the Upper Great Lakes region as NW flow 
impinges on the anomalous heights. This should result in a gradual 
warming and drying trend Sunday into early next week.
